The Maxwellians — Oliver Heaviside, Geor._note: Informal college, not an institution: coheres around the Treatise after Maxwell's death (1879); effectively dissolves with Hertz's death (1894-01-01) and FitzGerald's (1901). Hunt 1991 periodizes 1879-1894.

Classical electromagnetism — the unified._note: Conceived = displacement current closes the loop (On Physical Lines of Force III); formulated = 1865 paper, where Maxwell COINS 'electromagnetic field'; the equations were called Hertz-Heaviside / Maxwell-Hertz (Einstein 1905 says 'Maxwell-Hertz') before 'Maxwell's equations' settled — the name attached decades after both births.

Faraday's FIELD / lines-of-force program._note: Conceived = 'magnetic curves' in the 1831 induction work; formulated = diamagnetism + magneto-optical rotation (1845) through 'On the Physical Character of the Lines of Magnetic Force' (1852); named = first recorded use of 'magnetic field' in Faraday's 1845 notebook.

The mathematical apparatus of continenta._note: Conceived = Coulomb's law (1785); formulated = Oersted (1820) -> Ampere's force law (1820-27) -> Gauss flux work -> Neumann's induction formalism (1845). Never carried ONE name — a tradition, not a christened theory (no 'named' field, honestly).

Displacement current (changing E sources._note: Conceived/derived inside the molecular-vortex model (On Physical Lines of Force, Part III); the term 'displacement current' is Maxwell's own, standard by the 1865 paper.

Vector calculus (div/grad/curl)._note: Conceived = Hamilton's quaternions (1843), the parent algebra; formulated = Gibbs's privately printed Elements of Vector Analysis (1881-84) + Heaviside's recast of Maxwell (1884-85); named/consolidated = Gibbs-Wilson 'Vector Analysis' textbook (1901).

Luminiferous ether._note: Conceived = Huygens's wave medium; formulated = Young/Fresnel wave optics; dissolved as ontology by special relativity 1905 after Michelson-Morley 1887, with rear-guard ether-drift work (Dayton Miller) into the late 1920s.
